name: NeoMutt
account: `neomutt -F harness/neomuttrc`, in a Ghostty window sized to the benchmark window. No setup: the rc file points it at the server and keeps its caches in ~/mailbench/neomutt.
parity: neomutt caches headers and fetches bodies when they are opened; the rc file sets both caches, so a message it has opened once is local from then on.
reset: Press Enter here, then start it again.

layout.note: A terminal client has no bundle of its own: the instrument finds the terminal hosting it by name, and the window title is set by neomutt. Launch and quit are not measured, because they would be the terminal's.

caveats.text: In the comparison for the floor, not the middle: a terminal client with no compositor, no layout engine and no list to virtualize is roughly the fastest a mail client can be on the hardware.
